daily.title: US Supreme Court denies Trump bid to restrict mail-in ballots
daily.summary: The court said election officials do not have sufficient time to implement the rule before the November midterms.

daily.title: Germany news: Merz urges CDU discipline as pressure grows
daily.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz has urged his party to stay disciplined as pressure grows over his leadership. Meanwhile, Germany's homeownership rate has fallen to its lowest level in 20 years. DW has the latest.

daily.title: Kremlin-linked Russian oligarch helped fund Trump Jr.'s wedding celebration
daily.summary: Trump's son and his wife confirmed reports that Umar Kremlev paid for parts of the festivities. Kremlev was awarded the "Order of Friendship" by Putin earlier this year.

daily.title: Arctic power plays: EU searches for a new strategy
daily.summary: Russia’s aggression, Trump’s threats against Greenland and the race for critical raw materials are pushing the Arctic to the top of Europe’s agenda.

daily.title: Ukraine, Russia set for new round of US-mediated talks
daily.summary: New trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US could begin in October, according to Kyiv and Moscow. Few expect a breakthrough, but Ukraine is seeking a partial de-escalation to help it get through the winter.

daily.title: Trump seeks halt to energy attacks by both Russia, Ukraine
daily.summary: Donald Trump, under fire for record US diesel prices, claims Russia and Ukraine have agreed to stop striking energy targets. Russia said nothing; Ukraine said "we expect specifics from our partners" on any such move.

daily.title: Donald Trump dismisses concerns about dangers of AI
daily.summary: The president called efforts to slow the development of artificial intelligence a "sick conspiracy," claiming they only serve China. Market leaders have warned of the dangers of the pace of the technology's development.

daily.title: Yemen's Houthis attack Saudis, seize crucial Red Sea islands
daily.summary: Iran-backed Houthi rebels have tightened their grip on a key shipping route, capturing two strategic Red Sea islands. The closure of another global transport route is the latest ripple effect of the US war with Iran.

daily.title: Women's Basketball World Cup: Can Germany harness a boom?
daily.summary: Germany thrilled fans at the Women's Basketball World Cup. But even if this sparked a boom in the women's game, the infrastructure simply isn't ready for it.

daily.title: IPO 'for the people' is out of reach for many in Nigeria
daily.summary: Dangote seeks $1.6 billion from investors to finance a $14.3 billion expansion and thus double the oil refinery's capacity. The offer could give millions of Nigerians a stake in the company. But who can truly afford it?

daily.title: Ukraine: AfD questions German aid, Berlin remains committed
daily.summary: Emboldened by its win in Saxony-Anhalt, the far-right Alternative for Germany wants the government to change its Ukraine and Russia policies. Berlin is staying the course, but support is fading — especially in the east.

daily.title: The Crusades: How a medieval Holy War still shapes politics
daily.summary: In 1095, the Catholic Church launched the Crusades: wars that left millions dead and whose legacy still shapes political and ideological conflicts.

daily.title: Nepal: thousands still missing as flood recovery begins
daily.summary: The Himalayan nation is moving from rescue operations to recovery, facing a $4.8 billion reconstruction bill amid renewed calls for climate justice.

daily.title: EU leaders urge unity after Russian strike on train
daily.summary: Russia's drone attack on a train near the Ukraine-Poland border has triggered EU calls to up support for Kyiv. Allies of Ukraine should show they "are not scared," said the bloc's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas.

daily.title: Berlin businesswoman charged with spying for Russia
daily.summary: Prosecutors say the Berlin marketing executive used her political and military contacts to help a Russian intelligence officer gain access to influential circles and seek information on German defense policy.

daily.title: India women's team refuse Asia Cup cricket trophy from Pakistan minister
daily.summary: After beating Sri Lanka to win a record eighth Asia Cup title, the Indian women's cricket team skipped the trophy presentation with Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi.

daily.title: Pay to ghost your boss: Japan's resignation business
daily.summary: Resignation agencies in Japan help employees leave their jobs seamlessly in just 15 minutes. Young people are especially eager to use their services.

daily.title: Israeli minister accuses 'NAZA' filmmakers of 'treason'
daily.summary: Israel's culture minister wants to strip the makers of a documentary on Israel's Gaza offensive of their citizenship. He accused the two of seeking "applause from antisemites around the world."

daily.title: Finland: EU leaders meet to forge new Arctic policy
daily.summary: European leaders are meeting over shipping, resources and security in the region amid pressure from the US, China and Russia. The EU sees the Arctic as key to its future security as melting ice makes it more accessible.

daily.title: North Korea says recent drill shows 'huge destructive power'
daily.summary: North Korea carried out a coordinated live-fire exercise involving multiple weapons systems over the weekend. The drill came after the US, South Korea and Japan wrapped up five days of joint maritime exercises.

daily.title: Can Iran replace sea trade with land routes?
daily.summary: Iran is shifting trade toward northern ports and land routes as its southern shipping faces a US blockade. Analysts say the corridors can keep essential goods moving, but cannot replace maritime trade.

daily.title: In cosmopolitan Berlin, elections still closed to foreigners
daily.summary: A quarter of Berlin residents will have no say in the German capital's city-state election because they lack citizenship. That's the highest proportion of residents excluded from the election yet, and many are unhappy.

daily.title: Germany: Merz's CDU comes out on top in Lower Saxony polls
daily.summary: The Christian Democrats have emerged as the strongest party following local elections in the state of Lower Saxony. The vote was closely watched as an indicator of the strength of the far-right AfD, which came in third.

weekly.title: Germany's Zverev wins US Open in golden year
weekly.summary: Alexander Zverev has won the US Open for the first time, defeating Ben Shelton in the final. It is Zverev's second Grand Slam win of 2026 after a long wait for his first title, but controversy still hangs over him.

weekly.title: Russians on the Goethe-Institut: 'Hostage to politics'
weekly.summary: Canceled language exams, disrupted plans to study in Germany and the disappearance of an important cultural link: DW users shared how the closure of Germany's Goethe-Institut in Russia has affected their lives.

weekly.title: A Romani artist in Hungary reclaims his identity
weekly.summary: Norbert Olah is an artist. He's also Romani. For a long time, he avoided making his ethnic background a theme of his art for fear of being pigeonholed. Then it became his focus.

weekly.title: Why are European banks moving gold out of United States?
weekly.summary: The Netherlands and France have moved their gold out of US vaults. Part of the reason is fears about the reliability of the US, but equally important is the need to keep gold closer to home in the event of a crisis.

weekly.title: Corals as climate archive: Are El Nino events intensifying?
weekly.summary: Records show that El Nino events have been frequent and often extreme over the past few decades. Is this normal? Or is it the result of climate change? Corals can give us a clear indication.

weekly.title: Russia's drone war comes to Moldova and Romania
weekly.summary: Incursions by Russian drones into Moldovan and Romanian airspace are increasingly common. This week the Ukrainian president's plane was stopped from taking off from Chisinau. Observers suspect the attacks are deliberate.

weekly.title: DW exclusive: Zelenskyy offers to meet Putin at G20 in Miami
weekly.summary: In an interview with DW, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country was in a strong position to negotiate and offered to meet Vladimir Putin in Miami.

weekly.title: India looks to steer BRICS away from anti-Western turn
weekly.summary: The BRICS summit 2026 takes place in Delhi this weekend. Unlike last year, Putin and Xi are expected to attend. Can India keep the expanded bloc united?

weekly.title: Turks in Germany anxious after AfD wins in Saxony-Anhalt
weekly.summary: The Alternative for Germany party's win in Saxony-Anhalt has alarmed people of Turkish origin in eastern states. Will workers and business owners abandon the increasingly AfD-friendly region for the more welcoming west?

weekly.title: The 'end of an era' as Goethe-Institut in Russia closes
weekly.summary: The Goethe-Institut was one of the last German institutions still operating in Russia. However, following Moscow's decision to close its offices, all employees will have to stop working by September 13.

weekly.title: Magyar vs. Moscow: Hungary toughens stance toward Russia
weekly.summary: Prime Minister Peter Magyar has abruptly ended the era of his predecessor's warm relations with Russia: Hungary has expelled 10 Russian diplomats. The Kremlin is considering halting gas supplies in response.

weekly.title: Germany sets its sights on Russia's shadow fleet
weekly.summary: The German government wants to follow other EU countries and take more decisive action against Russia's shadow fleet, accusing it of helping Moscow evade sanctions and carry out acts of sabotage.

weekly.title: Cyberattack in Berlin: 1.4 million files on the dark web
weekly.summary: Shortly before Berlin's state parliamentary election, the hacker group Rhysida stole data, tried to extort the Berlin Senate and published the data on the dark web after their attempt failed.

weekly.title: How Celine Dion became a pop culture icon across generations
weekly.summary: As the global star kicks off her anticipated Paris residency, here's how Celine Dion managed to gain younger followers while keeping her loyal older fans.

weekly.title: Are electric cars really bad for the environment?
weekly.summary: Some German politicians are calling for a delay to the EU plan to phase out gas-powered vehicles, saying cars must be judged on the entire carbon footprint. But the full picture still says EVs are more climate friendly.

weekly.title: Serbia, the conflicted EU candidate
weekly.summary: On paper, Belgrade has pursued EU membership for years. But accession has long been stalled. The hero's farewell given to war criminal Mladic exposed just how far Serbia has alienated itself from Europe.

weekly.title: How Belarusians still find hope in a silenced country
weekly.summary: The documentary "Letters from the Silenced Country" depicts the ongoing repression under the authoritarian regime. Director Andrei Kutsila talked to DW ahead of the film's Venice premiere.

weekly.title: Why we're still looking for dark matter
weekly.summary: When physicists said they may have spotted evidence of dark matter almost 100 years after it was proposed as a theory, the internet lit up. Here's why we're searching for the thing that holds everything else together.

weekly.title: LIV Golf in financial turmoil: What's next for the sport?
weekly.summary: Six months after Saudi Arabia pulled funding from the breakaway organization, LIV Golf have filed for bankruptcy protection. Several of the world's best players signed on to LIV, so where does that leave golf?

weekly.title: Conspiracy theories can provide answers but not peace
weekly.summary: Twenty-five years after 9/11, conspiracy theories about the terrorist attacks persist. But even as an attempt to make sense of a tragedy, psychologists say the benefit in conspiracy ideation or belief is short-lived.

weekly.title: The billion-euro trade driving Europe's eels to extinction
weekly.summary: Traffickers are making big bucks smuggling millions of critically endangered eels across continents, using suitcases on planes and legal loopholes to deliver them to dinnerplates. Where are the smuggling hotspots?

weekly.title: The Bayeux Tapestry in London: What's behind the hype?
weekly.summary: The exhibition of the Bayeux Tapestry at the British Museum is eagerly anticipated across the UK, as the medieval masterpiece is considered by many to be a symbol of the country's identity.

weekly.title: EU sports commissioner says FIFA is 'damaging to football'
weekly.summary: Speaking to DW, EU Commissioner Glenn Micallef hit out at world football's governing body over its "poor governance."

weekly.title: Putin rejects mobilization rumors, many Russians unconvinced
weekly.summary: Russia’s President Vladimir Putin has dismissed rumors about military mobilization. But many Russians, including many DW users, say they are preparing for the possibility.

weekly.title: German economy frets about Saxony-Anhalt election results
weekly.summary: The AfD won the election in the eastern German state by a wide margin. While politicians and election analysts are still debating the reasons for the far-right party's popularity, economists are sounding the alarm.

weekly.title: Ratko Mladic’s funeral casts shadow over Bosnia and Herzegovina vote
weekly.summary: Ratko Mladic’s funeral in Belgrade, attended by Serbian and Bosnian Serb leaders, has deepened regional tensions and could affect the upcoming election in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

weekly.title: BSW and AfD – a political love-hate relationship in Germany
weekly.summary: The Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW) could help the Alternative for Germany (AfD) into power in Saxony-Anhalt. But the BSW is riddled with infighting

weekly.title: Afghanistan's women: A national soccer team without a home
weekly.summary: The Afghan women's national football team has finally been officially recognized by FIFA. Now the players want to make history both on and off the field.

weekly.title: PISA 2025 results: Reading and math scores plummet worldwide
weekly.summary: The PISA 2025 results reveal record-low student performance, with digital distractions and AI use raising concerns. Germany is faring worse than ever.

weekly.title: Elversberg: Bundesliga newcomers from tiny town make waves
weekly.summary: A team from a small southwestern German town of just 7,000 inhabitants made history by sealing promotion to become the 59th club to play in the Bundesliga. Elversberg has got off to a memorable start.

weekly.title: Egg freezing in women's football: Choice or pressure?
weekly.summary: Spain's football federation is set to join a handful of clubs in paying for female players to freeze their eggs. Experts have welfare concerns.
